common.applies_to: Established bush rose (Hybrid Tea, Floribunda, provisional Grandiflora); dormant pruning
common.preserved_uncertainty: No source describes what a rubbing wound looks like; the rubbing/crossing distinction below is an approved default, not a sourced finding. No beginner lookalike list exists (SC §6). Whether crossing and inward-growing stems usually occur together is unknown (SC §6).

content.look_for: Next, let's look for stems that cross each other or rub together.

criteria.text: A stem crossing another is a candidate. Crossing and rubbing are looked for together.
Bark damage, wear or a flattened face where two stems touch: treat as rubbing.
Stems close together with no contact or wear: treat as crossing, not rubbing.

content.photo_limit: One photo can't reliably show whether two stems actually touch. Look from several sides.
content.confirm_question: Follow both stems with your hands. Do they cross or touch?
content.not_sure_guidance: Take another photo from a different angle, and look again from another side.
content.any_more_question: Can you see any more crossing or rubbing stems?
